note: Editorial copy only. Every number on the site is generated from results/ by scripts/build_site.py. Do not put measurements in this file.

site.name: WhichJudge
site.headline: You don't need a better model. You need a quit line.
site.descriptionTemplate: Independent bake-off of cheap in-loop decision models on {tasks} decisions: Jev vs gpt-4o-mini vs {modern} vs TF-IDF, n={nmin}-{nmax} frozen gold, full per-call receipts.

tasks.title: Prompt-injection screen
tasks.replaces: LLM guard deciding whether untrusted input may reach an agent
tasks.dataset: deepset/prompt-injections, train + test, multilingual, n=200 (rows left after v1)
tasks.why: Jev 80.5% against Mini 74.5% is a significant 6.0pt win (Holm p=0.036), and it does not matter: Jev misses 39.0% of injections, Mini 51.0%, the 2026 model 28.0%, all at 0.0% false positives. TF-IDF at 90.5% beats both APIs. A security gate is judged on what gets through, and every model here lets a third or more through.
tasks.gate: At >=0.9: 86.3% on 84.0% of rows, 5.8pt above ungated. Recall of injections on the covered rows barely moves, so raising the bar hands the misses to a human instead of catching them.
tasks.goldNote: Curated research corpus, predates current agent tooling
tasks.rowNote: Misses 39.0% of injections at any threshold. TF-IDF beats both APIs at 90.5%.

tasks.title: Consumer complaint routing
tasks.replaces: LLM classifier routing inbound financial complaints to a product queue
tasks.dataset: CFPB Consumer Complaint Database, 8 product queues
tasks.labels: credit_reporting / debt_collection / cards / bank_account / mortgage / money_transfer / loans / student_loan
tasks.why: The only row here that is not academic gold: a regulator runs this routing live and the consumer writes the narrative. Jev 83.8% beats Mini 77.4% by 6.4pt (Holm p=0.0002). TF-IDF scores 85.6%, ns against Jev and significant against Mini; the 2026 model ties Jev at 83.8%. Narratives average about 960 characters, past the cost crossover, so Jev is the cheaper API by the widest margin on the board: $33.42 against $78.59 per million decisions.
tasks.gate: At >=0.9: 92.1% on 78.6% of complaints, 8.3pt above ungated. ECE 0.094 means do not repeat the confidence to anyone as a probability; it does not stop you thresholding on it.
tasks.goldNote: Live system: a regulator routes these daily and the filer picks the label
tasks.rowNote: Replace is vs Mini only. TF-IDF scores 85.6%, ns vs Jev; the 2026 model ties Jev.

tasks.title: Comment toxicity gate
tasks.replaces: Toxicity classifier gating user comments before publication
tasks.why: A neighbour of the hate-speech row: toxicity in comments rather than hate speech aimed at a group in tweets, on CC0 gold. Jev 76.8% beats Mini 72.4% (Holm p=0.035). TF-IDF beats both at 85.2%. Read this next to the hate row: a different task and dataset gives a different ranking, which is the point, not proof that the hate loss was label noise.
tasks.gate: 86.7% on 58.8% of comments at >=0.9, 9.9pt above ungated, and ECE 0.101 is low enough to state the confidence out loud. Publish that slice automatically and queue the rest.
tasks.goldNote: Real content from a news site, labels from crowd annotators
tasks.rowNote: Misses 33.2% of toxic comments; Mini misses 40.0%. TF-IDF beats both at 85.2%.

tasks.title: SMS spam gate
tasks.replaces: Spam vs ham classifier on inbound SMS
tasks.why: Dead heat: Jev 95.4%, Mini 94.6%, TF-IDF 96.0%, the 2026 model 93.0%. Nothing separates the four after correction. Classical ML is enough here.
tasks.gate: At >=0.9: 98.6% on 86.0% of messages, 3.2pt above ungated, with ECE 0.015, the best-calibrated row on the board. Automate the slice, queue the rest.

tasks.title: Review polarity
tasks.dataset: SST-2 validation, the 356 rows left after v1
tasks.why: Tied: Jev 96.3% vs Mini 95.5% (Holm p=1). TF-IDF drops to 84.8%, so the models earn their keep against classical, not against each other. n=356 because v1 used the rest of the split.
tasks.gate: At >=0.8: 97.9% on 93.3% of reviews, 1.5pt above ungated. There is no headroom left, and ECE 0.030 says the confidence may be quoted.

tasks.title: Message emotion
tasks.dataset: tweet_eval emotion, train split (test exhausted by v1)
tasks.why: Tied after correction: Jev 78.2%, Mini 76.2%, the 2026 model 76.2% (Holm p=1). v1 had this as a Replace on the label-names-only prompt; with the same rubric on both sides the gap is 2.0pt and not significant. Optimism is still the weak class: Jev catches 62.4% of it, Mini 52.0%. TF-IDF trails at 60.0%.
tasks.gate: At >=0.9: 88.8% on 64.2% of messages, 10.6pt above ungated. ECE 0.100: threshold on it, do not quote it.
tasks.rowNote: v1 called this Replace; on equal prompts it is a tie.

tasks.title: Offensive language screen
tasks.dataset: tweet_eval offensive, train split (test exhausted by v1)
tasks.why: Jev 72.6%, Mini 72.2%, the 2026 model 73.6%, TF-IDF 69.4%: nothing separates them. Every model misses about a third of the offensive posts (Jev 35.6%, Mini 36.0%).
tasks.gate: At >=0.9: 81.4% on 59.0% of posts, 8.8pt above ungated. ECE 0.151: threshold, do not quote.

tasks.title: Social sentiment (3-way)
tasks.why: Tied: Jev 73.2%, Mini 71.4%, the 2026 model 71.0% (Holm p=1). Neutral is the hard class for all three; Jev catches 53.9% of it. TF-IDF trails at 60.2%.
tasks.gate: At >=0.9: 79.8% on 61.4% of messages, 6.6pt above ungated. ECE 0.157 is too high to quote the number; thresholding still works.

tasks.title: News topic
tasks.why: Jev 89.8% beats Mini 86.0% by 3.8pt (Holm p=0.025), and the 2026 model at 86.8% ties Jev. TF-IDF at 93.8% after training on 120k rows beats both APIs. If you have labels, skip both.
tasks.gate: Jev first among APIs. At >=0.9: 94.0% on 87.4% of articles, 4.2pt above ungated, ECE 0.068.
tasks.rowNote: Replace is vs Mini only. TF-IDF beats both at 93.8%.

tasks.title: Banking queue routing
tasks.dataset: BANKING77 train split, collapsed 77 to 8 queues
tasks.labels: cards / top_up / cash_atm / transfers / fx / account / payments_fees / other
tasks.why: TF-IDF 94.2% beats both neural judges by more than 20 points if you have labels. Among APIs Jev 70.2% beats Mini 66.4% (Holm p=0.021) and ties the 2026 model at 72.4%. The 'other' queue is the failure: Jev routes 1.6% of it correctly. Do not pay for a model on this task if you can train one.
tasks.gate: Gating works here even though the calibration does not: at >=0.9 it is 79.0% on 80.2% of tickets, 8.9pt above ungated. What ECE 0.232 costs you is the right to quote the confidence as a probability, not the right to threshold on it.
tasks.goldNote: Research corpus of customer queries, intents collapsed by keyword
tasks.rowNote: Replace is vs Mini only. TF-IDF beats both at 94.2%.

tasks.title: Hate-speech screen
tasks.why: Mini 72.4% beats Jev 65.6% by 6.8pt (Holm p=0.002), the same loss as v1 on equal prompts. Jev catches only 47.6% of hate speech; Mini 64.0%, the 2026 model 75.2% but with 33.2% false positives. TF-IDF is worst at 53.4%. The neighbouring Civil Comments row, a different task on CC0 gold, ranks the models the other way.
tasks.gate: Gating buys the most lift on the board and still leaves a bad row: 78.9% on 53.0% at >=0.9, 13.3pt above ungated, and Mini is better anyway. Keep a specialist.
tasks.rowNote: Misses 52.4% of hate speech. Don't is this dataset's verdict.

reproduce.heading: Reproduce this and I will publish your numbers
reproduce.body: Receipts prove I did not edit my own table. They cannot prove the APIs said it, because in principle I could have written the receipts. Only someone else re-running it fixes that. Clone the repo, add your own keys, run scripts/run_eval.py, and send me the summary.json diff. It costs about $0.12 in API calls. Confirmed runs get a reproduced-by line on the row, credited however you want.
reproduce.subject: WhichJudge reproduction

contribute.heading: Have labelled data for a real decision?
contribute.body: Nine of the eleven rows are public academic gold: comparable, but not production. Only CFPB complaint routing rests on a live system's own labels, and only Civil Comments uses real user text. The decisions worth measuring are the ones people actually run: support-queue routing, injection screening, PR risk gating, refund eligibility. Those need labelled examples and almost nobody publishes them. If you have a few hundred rows you can share, or a public set worth adding, I will measure it and publish the row. Your data does not get republished unless you say so.
